name: Hotel D'Angleterre Copenhagen
positioning: Historic grand hotel on Kongens Nytorv in the heart of Copenhagen, officially d'Angleterre, with roots going back to 1755 and a building that balances Victorian architecture with contemporary Nordic design
best_for: Travelers who want a central Copenhagen base within walking distance of Amalienborg Castle, Christiansborg and Tivoli Gardens
Guests who enjoy Champagne bars, art and grand historic interiors
Families who want baby and children amenities and concierge-planned outings such as LEGOLAND Billund

facts.text: The hotel is on Kongens Nytorv, in the heart of Copenhagen.
The nearest metro stop, Kongens Nytorv, is steps from the hotel entrance, and the metro runs directly to Copenhagen Airport in about 15 minutes.
Amalienborg Castle, The Marble Church, Christiansborg, Tivoli Gardens and Strøget can be reached on foot.
The name Hotel d'Angleterre, French for The England Hotel, came from The English Club hosted by owner Gottfried Rau.
The building balances stately Victorian architecture and contemporary Nordic design.
When the weather allows, the restaurant Marchal extends onto the terrace and sidewalk of Kongens Nytorv.
Breakfast is served in Marchal with a view over Kongens Nytorv.
Room service is available around the clock.
The hotel is fully wheelchair accessible, with elevators to all floors.
The hotel's art collection includes an original Andy Warhol.
The hotel offers baby and children amenities such as a baby cot, high chair, baby bathtub and toys, on advance request.
The hotel was awarded Two MICHELIN Keys in the 2026 MICHELIN Guide selection.

highlights.text: In 2001 the glass artist Albano Poli gave the Palm Court a mosaic roof, which the hotel describes as the biggest mosaic roof in Northern Europe.
Balthazar Champagne Bar offers more than 200 Champagnes, caviar service and live DJs on weekends.
Alfred Hitchcock's film Torn Curtain was filmed at the hotel.
The hotel has a private pool and spa managed by the holistic spa and skincare concept Amazing Space.
The hotel's history dates to 1755, when Jean Marchal and Maria Coppy founded a restaurant that later turned into a luxury hotel.

considerations.text: Dogs are not allowed in Marchal, the bar area or Balthazar Champagne Bar, but are welcome in the Upper Lobby.
WhataHotel notes premium luxury pricing that reflects the hotel's exclusive positioning.
